classification.difficultyReason: Simplify the quotient while retaining the original denominator restrictions, find all three excluded inputs, and represent them as holes on a constant graph. The explicit hint signals that cancellation alone is insufficient.

inlines.text: This is not simply the graph of
. There is more to it than that!

answer.short: $y=1$ for $x\in(-\pi,0)\cup(0,\pi)$, with open circles at $(-\pi,1)$, $(0,1)$ and $(\pi,1)$.
answer.worked: $\frac{\sin x}{\sin x}=1$ wherever $\sin x\ne0$. In the stated interval, $\sin x=0$ at $x=-\pi,0,\pi$, so the original expression is undefined at those values. Draw the horizontal line $y=1$ over the remaining domain and mark all three excluded points with open circles.

spec.description: Horizontal graph at y=1 with open circles at minus pi, zero and pi. Half-pi horizontal ticks and y=1 label are retained.
